- For AWS co-sell, the listing needs an explicit "partner sell-with" entitlement mapping in the product metadata and a co-sell playbook PDF that explains deal handoff. We can provide the playbook but we need your sales contact who will accept handoffs.

I can take point on the playbook and the entitlement mapping metadata. Action items:

Ben / Grace / Tom,

Quick technical note after reviewing the sku_mapping.xlsx (thanks Grace):

- Per-instance hourly metering is supported by Redwood's Dedicated and Hosted runtimes. For Hosted we can surface an "instance-hour" metric per customer account used by the marketplace metering adapter. For per-account ingest MB we already emit a usage metric.
- The tricky part is making the buyer-facing bundle behave like a single SKU in the marketplace while routing usage to two different metering APIs (hours + MB). Marketplaces expect a single metered dimension per SKU for automatic billing. Two options:
  1) Create a composite bundle SKU (marketplace-level) that maps to a single anchor metering dimension and have Redwood bill/settle the split internally (requires Redwood to be listed as the bill-to partner for the bundle).
  2) Publish the bundle as two linked SKUs: "Runtime Hourly" (metered by hours) + "Ingest Add-on" (metered by MB) and use marketplace entitlements to present them as a single purchase flow. This is more manual but aligns to AWS/GCP market constraints.

Recommendation: option 2 is lower friction for certification and faster to get to co-sell because it avoids changing bill-to relationships. If ACME really needs single-charge behavior we can scope a small integration to reconcile charges post-purchase (adds ~4 weeks).

I'll attach a quick diagram and a proposed short checklist for the marketplace mapping. If we go option 2, engineering asks: a) confirm SKU ids, b) provide a sandbox account for e2e verification, c) agree on the entitlement mapping for co-sell handoffs.

-Karthik
